title: Offline-first packetized prefetch and commit protocol (PRD draft)
content:
Objective:
Provide an ergonomic SDK surface and server-side protocol that lets mobile/edge clients operate in offline or flaky networks while preserving low-latency tool-call SLOs, compact structured outputs, and resumable sessions. The design focuses on packetized prefetch, staged commit frames, and a small, explicit reconciliation model suitable for hosted API streaming with tool integration.

Context / motivation:
- Many customers embed Hosted API into clients with intermittent connectivity (mobile apps, kiosks, in-field devices). Current streaming + tool models assume always-online and break when networks drop or when tool latency spikes.
- We need a pragmatic tradeoff: keep server-side semantics simple enough to maintain strong cost/latency guarantees, while enabling clients to prefetch probable tool results, resume mid-response, and eventually reconcile authoritative outputs.

Key concepts (short):
- Packetized prefetch: server returns one or more small "packets" of partial outputs + prefetch hints. Each packet contains typed payloads (text, json fragment, tool-handle metadata). Clients can commit packets locally as provisional state.
- Staged commit frames: commits are explicit lightweight frames that mark a packet as authoritative for the client (provisional -> confirmed). The server tracks commit ids; commits can be optimistic or validated after backend tool resolution.
- Deferred tool adaptor: when a tool call is expensive (external search, db), server can return a tool-adaptor token in the packet and optionally a cached/soft result. Clients can speculatively show the soft result but must tag UI if result is provisional.
- Resume token: every packet includes a resume token allowing clients to resume a stream at packet granularity; robust to out-of-order arrival and duplication.

API surface sketches (client-centric):
- startSession({prompt, resumeToken?: string, prefetchBudget?: number}) -> stream of Packets
- Packet = {packet_id, resume_token, payloads: [typed-fragments], prefetch_hints: [tool_tokens], commit_window: number}
- commit(packet_id) -> commit_ack {commit_id, validation_state}
- reconcile(commit_id) -> finalization_event (optional async)

Behavioral guarantees:
- Low-latency path: best-effort packet delivery and local provisional commits for interactive UX. Prefetch hints should keep additional token cost minimal and be bounded by client-specified prefetchBudget.
- Safety: any UI surfaces showing provisional tool results must include provenance metadata (provisional=true, expected-staleness). Final commit frames replace provisional data and produce telemetry events for quality checks.
- Cost controls: server enforces per-session prefetchBudget and per-tool-rate limits; prefetch is billed separately and surfaced in Console metrics.

SDK ergonomics notes:
- Minimal surface: expose packets and commit API; avoid forcing app devs to reason about low-level byte streams. Provide helper classes: PacketBuffer (handles dedupe + resume), CommitPromise (retries commit until ack or timeout), ToolStub (manages provisional UI + fallback).
- Mobile-first optimizations: small default packet size, configurable backoff on network re-connect, pre-warm resume token on app foreground.
- Local dev tools: a simulator binary that returns canned packets with delayed tool-adaptor responses to test offline flows.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: emit events for prefetch usage, provisional->final flips, commit latencies, tool-adaptor timeouts.
- Rollout: start as an opt-in flag for selected customers; expose usage dashboard in Console under "Prefetch".
- Fallbacks: if commits repeatedly fail, client should fall back to full synchronous request (non-prefetched) or show an error CTA.

Open questions / risks:
- UX complexity: how much responsibility should app devs have for marking provisional UI? Provide native UI components?
- Tool correctness: speculative prefetch may surface stale results; need regression tests and quality alerts.
- Billing model: separate prefetch billing vs generation billing — communicate clearly in Console and invoices.

Next steps (short roadmap):
- Spike: implement server-side packetizer + resume token generator (2 sprints).
- SDK: mobile JS/Swift/Kotlin PacketBuffer + CommitPromise prototypes (1 sprint).
- Field test: onboard 2 beta apps from CS that need offline capability (4 weeks).
- Metrics: add prefetch KPI to Optimize product hooks and Console (concurrent).

Notes to reviewers:
- See linked GH PR for experimental packet format.
- Questions inline in TODO: markers in the appendix (end of doc) — please add comments in Drive.

Appendix (TODO checklist and quick sketches):
- TODO: define wire encoding (jsonl vs protobuf) — prefer small protobuf for mobile efficiency.
- TODO: prefetchBudget semantics (tokens vs calls) and default thresholds.
- TODO: contract for tool-adaptor tokens: expiry and idempotency hints.
- Quick sketch: UI component should expose .isProvisional flag and onCommit replacement callback.

Rough sign-off criteria:
- Packetized protocol implemented server-side with resume tokens and commit acks.
- SDKs provide PacketBuffer + CommitPromise and one mobile UI example.
- Console shows prefetch usage and provisional->final flip rates.
